title: Replacing a Post Light: Aluminum Post, LED Diode Fixture, and Time-Clock Control
summary: This Old House documents a front-yard lighting upgrade focused on replacing a failing exterior post light. After identifying a faulty wall switch and a deteriorating lamppost, the project replaces the post with a 7-foot aluminum model, installs a new LED diode fixture (no replaceable bulb) with a diffuser, and routes wiring through the post using dry-mix concrete for a quick-set footing. The update includes upgrading the electrical box to a weatherproof unit, pulling new wiring to a weatherproof outdoor switch, and installing an astronomical time clock to automate dusk-to-dawn lighting. To finish, the installer replaces a matching wall sconce to harmonize with the new post light. The video emphasizes durability, weatherproofing, and a cohesive exterior lighting design that complements the house and railing.
topics: aluminum post (3 inch diameter, 7 feet tall)

sections.title: Assessment and planning: identifying switch and post issues
concepts: faulty wall switch that powers a lamppost
decision to replace switch and post
sections.description: The host notes a switch on the wall that powers the lamppost; when released, the light goes off, indicating a probable faulty switch. The lamppost itself is described as rusted and unstable, with a keeled-over bulb. The plan emerges to replace both the switch and the post and to upgrade nearby exterior lighting styling.

sections.title: Removal of old post and installation of new post
concepts: new post specifications (3-inch diameter, 7 feet tall)
sections.description: After clearing vegetation, the old post is removed, making way for a new standard aluminum post. The new post is specified as 3 inches in diameter and 7 feet tall, designed to accept various fixtures and resist rust.

sections.title: Wiring, footing, and initial assembly
concepts: wire routing through a side hole in the post
sections.description: Wiring is threaded through a dedicated hole in the post while a quick-set, dry-mix concrete is poured into the footing. The footing is allowed to set, providing a sturdy base for the new post.

sections.title: Electrical upgrades, fixture wiring, and automation
concepts: new wiring to support a post light and switch
astronomical time clock for dusk-to-dawn operation
sections.description: The old non-code box is replaced with a weatherproof exterior box, and wiring is updated to feed a new switch. An astronomical time clock is installed to automate lighting, with a diffuser added to the LED fixture for softer illumination. A weatherproof cover is placed over the control hardware.

sections.title: Finish and test: power restoration and design polish
concepts: matching sconce to the new post light
sections.description: Power is reconnected and the new post light is tested. A matching wall sconce is installed to complement the post light, completing a cohesive exterior lighting aesthetic.
